site.name: fleetatlas
site.summary: FleetAtlas Fictional commercial fleet real-time management SaaS dashboard, used as a UXBench fixture. Pages - `index.html` — Fleet overview map home. Left thin rail nav; top bar with org switcher, view tabs (Map / List / Analytics), search box, alert bell (dropdown shows the 5 most recent on click); status filter strip (All / Running / Idle / Maintenance / Offline / Alert); full-screen SVG city map with 25 vehicles in real-time positions (running vehicles jitter their position every 5 seconds to simulate live updates); clicking a vehicle icon or drawer row → right detail panel slides in; bottom pull-up drawer showing the vehicle list. - Right detail panel (controlled by JS within the map page) — basic info (plate / model / year / VIN / fleet), driver info (with phone / shift / accumulated drive hours), current task (route / location / ETA / remaining miles), historical track SVG (24h / 7d / 30d toggle), fuel and speed sparklines; 4 action buttons (Send command / Contact driver / Maintenance record / Reassign task), with Reassign being a destructive action that has a second-confirmation modal. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPI cards (open / new today / by severity / mean handli

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full fleetatlas system, prioritizing the primary dashboard flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The FleetAtlas system suffers from critical layout and interaction failures on mobile devices, rendering the primary vehicle management workflows unusable. The desktop experience is severely compromised by a persistent sidebar overlay that intercepts pointer events, blocking access to filters and action buttons across multiple pages. While data visualization is present, the lack of responsive adaptation and inaccessible touch targets creates significant friction for fleet managers attempting to monitor or reassign vehicles.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of FleetAtlas, focusing on the real-time dashboard interaction model, data consistency across views (Map/List/Analytics), and the efficiency of critical workflows like alert resolution and vehicle reassignment.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will begin with the primary Dashboard flow, validating map interactivity, view switching, and the vehicle detail panel. It will then move to adjacent pages (Vehicles, Alerts, Analytics) to check for data parity and filtering capabilities. Finally, it will stress-test high-risk interactions like destructive actions (Reassign) and mobile responsiveness given the identified layout warnings.
assumptions: The 'Drivers', 'Routes', 'Maintenance', and 'Settings' links in the sidebar are placeholders (#) and do not lead to functional pages based on prescan hrefs.
The 'Reassign task' action triggers a confirmation modal as described in the site summary.
Real-time updates (jittering vehicles) occur automatically without user intervention.
risk_hotspots: Right detail panel: Complexity of information density (Driver info + Task + History + Sparklines).
Reassign Task button: Destructive action requiring confirmation modal validation.
Mobile Viewport: Prescan indicates multiple tap targets < 44px (sidebar nav, view toggles).
Alert Bell Dropdown: Interaction design for quick access vs. full page navigation.

phases.title: Dashboard Core & Map Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the primary real-time monitoring experience, including map controls, view switching, and status filtering.
key_checks: Click individual vehicle icons on the map to open the Right Detail Panel.
Verify content in Detail Panel: Plate, Driver, Current Task, and Sparklines.
Toggle between 'Map view', 'List view', and 'Analytics view' tabs within the dashboard.
Apply status filters (e.g., 'Running', 'Alert') and verify list/map updates.
Interact with the Alert Bell icon to check the dropdown preview.
exit_criteria: Successfully opened and closed at least 3 different vehicle detail panels.
Confirmed that status filters reduce the visible vehicle count appropriately.
Verified that 'List view' tab displays the same data structure as the bottom drawer.

phases.title: Critical Workflows & Destructive Actions
phases.objective: Test complex interactions involving modals and multi-step processes, specifically focusing on safety-critical or destructive actions.
key_checks: Open a vehicle detail panel and click 'Reassign task'.
Validate the appearance and behavior of the second-confirmation modal.
Test 'Cancel' vs. 'Confirm' paths in the modal.
Click 'Contact driver' and 'Send command' to check for feedback/toasts (even if simulated).
Search for a specific vehicle using the top search bar ('Search by plate / driver...').
exit_criteria: Confirmation modal for 'Reassign task' appears and functions correctly.
Search functionality filters the vehicle list effectively.
Action buttons provide some form of UI feedback (modal, toast, or state change).

phases.title: Adjacent Pages & Data Consistency
phases.objective: Ensure data integrity and consistent filtering/search patterns across the dedicated sub-pages.
key_checks: Navigate to 'Vehicles' page: Check table sorting and filtering by fleet/status.
Navigate to 'Alerts' page: Verify KPI cards match the dashboard bell count (12).
Test alert filtering (Severity, Type, Status) and 'Assign' action.
Navigate to 'Analytics' page: Review heatmap and driver performance tables.
Cross-reference a vehicle's status on 'Vehicles' page with its status on the Dashboard.
exit_criteria: Confirmed that 'Open alerts' count on alerts.html matches the badge on index.html.
Verified that filtering controls on sub-pages behave consistently with the dashboard.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Accessibility
phases.objective: Identify usability issues on smaller screens, focusing on the tap target warnings found in the prescan.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE or Pixel 5).
Attempt to tap sidebar navigation items (identified as < 44px height).
Check legibility of the Map view and Vehicle List on mobile.
Test the 'Alerts' page filter dropdowns on mobile (often prone to overflow).
Verify if the Right Detail Panel becomes a full-screen overlay or bottom sheet on mobile.
exit_criteria: Documented any unclickable elements due to small size.
Verified if the layout breaks or becomes unusable on narrow viewports.
Checked if horizontal scrolling is required for tables on mobile.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 4 known HTML files (index, vehicles, alerts, analytics).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise Map interactions, Detail Panel actions (especially Reassign), Global Search, and Status Filters.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 3 key checks on mobile viewport to validate touch targets.

notes: Prescan flagged 'missing_input_label' on the org switcher select box; verify if this persists in screen reader testing or visual layout.
The 'Drivers', 'Routes', etc. links are likely dead ends; do not spend steps trying to navigate them unless they show unexpected behavior.
Pay attention to the 'real-time' aspect: observe if vehicle positions update or if 'Last update' timestamps change during the session.

findings.user_goal: View and manage vehicle lists on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Severe horizontal overflow and layout breakage on mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: On `vehicles.html` (mobile), the page width is 916px while the viewport is only 390px. This forces users to horizontally scroll to see critical columns like 'Status', 'Location', and the 'Details' action button. The map view on `index.html` also exhibits 751px width overflow, clipping content.
findings.why_it_matters: Fleet managers often work in the field using mobile devices. Requiring horizontal scrolling to access basic data or actions violates core mobile UX principles, leading to high cognitive load, missed information, and frustration.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive table design that stacks columns vertically or hides non-essential columns behind a 'more details' expansion on mobile. Ensure the map container scales to fit the viewport width without overflow.

findings.user_goal: Filter vehicles by status or assign alerts.
findings.problem: Left sidebar overlay intercepts pointer events, blocking interaction with main content controls.
findings.evidence: Multiple click actions failed on `vehicles.html`, `alerts.html`, and `index.html` because the `<aside class="sidebar">` and its children (e.g., 'Settings', 'Vehicles' links) are visually overlapping or logically intercepting clicks intended for dropdowns (like 'All statuses') and buttons (like 'Assign' or 'Details').
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot perform essential tasks such as filtering the vehicle list or assigning alerts. This is a complete blockage of functionality, making the application appear broken or unresponsive.
findings.suggestion: Fix the z-index stacking context so the sidebar sits strictly behind the main content area, or ensure the main content area has sufficient left-margin/padding to prevent overlap. Verify that the sidebar does not capture pointer events when it is not explicitly open or focused.

findings.user_goal: Use screen readers or keyboard navigation to filter data.
findings.problem: Form controls lack accessible labels, aria-labels, or placeholders.
findings.evidence: The organization selector ('Aurora Logistics Group'), status filters ('All statuses...'), and fleet filters ('All fleets...') on `vehicles.html` and `alerts.html` are `<select>` elements without associated `<label>` tags, `aria-label` attributes, or visible placeholder text that describes their function to assistive technologies.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear generic 'combo box' announcements without context, making it impossible to understand what is being filtered. This violates WCAG accessibility standards and excludes users with disabilities.
findings.suggestion: Add visible `<label>` elements for all form controls. If visual space is tight, use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to provide descriptive names for screen readers.

findings.user_goal: Tap action buttons and filters accurately on a touchscreen.
findings.problem: Touch targets are significantly smaller than the recommended 44x44px minimum.
findings.evidence: On `vehicles.html` (mobile), the 'Details' button is 57x26px (height < 44px). Checkboxes in the table are 13x13px. Navigation links in the sidebar are 41px high. The user profile icon is 36x36px.
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets lead to frequent mis-taps, especially for users with larger fingers or those using the device in motion (e.g., a driver or field manager). This increases error rates and task completion time.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding of all interactive elements to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px. For small icons like checkboxes, increase the clickable area via CSS padding without necessarily changing the visual size of the icon itself.

findings.user_goal: Understand why a click action failed.
findings.problem: Lack of visual feedback when interactions are blocked or fail.
findings.evidence: When the agent attempted to click 'Details' or filters and the sidebar intercepted the event, there was no visual indication (such as a cursor change, highlight, or error toast) to the user that the click was registered but blocked. The interface simply remained static.
findings.why_it_matters: Silent failures cause confusion and make users doubt the system's reliability. They may repeatedly click the same element, leading to frustration.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that if an element is obscured or disabled, the cursor reflects this state. If an action fails due to a system error, provide a brief notification or visual cue indicating the issue.
